subject: Dedicated reservation — sprint activation & minimal floor options
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@terminusbio.com>; Dr. Ethan Shaw <ethan.shaw@terminusbio.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 04 Jun 2028 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated reservation — sprint activation & minimal floor options

Hi Aisha / Ethan —

Thanks again for the deep dive last week. Attached is a concise plan (terminus_dedicated_plan_v1.pdf) that maps a recommended dedicated cluster and a conservative minimum floor that aligns with the product QA sprint you described. High level here: 

- Recommended baseline cluster: 48 x A100-equivalent GPUs (configured as two 24-GPU lanes for traffic isolation).
- Minimum reserved floor: 12 GPUs (kept warm for low-latency inference).
- Ramp schedule (proposed):
  * Week 0–4: 12 min floor active + 24 GPUs burstable (pilot lane).
  * Month 2: increase to 24 reserved GPUs as model evaluation passes performance gates.
  * Month 4–6: target 48 reserved GPUs aligned to high-throughput production traffic.
- Burst strategy: Shared burst pool enables up to 80 GPUs for short windows (automated billing guardrails).
- Canary / warm-start: We recommend a 72-hour warm window before each stage increase to prime KV caches and avoid cold penalties.

Cost and commercial notes are summarized on page 3 of the PDF. Two items I want to flag now: 1) we can reduce the minimum floor to 8 GPUs if you require greater downward flexibility, but that will increase reliance on burst capacity for peak spikes; 2) we can structure a 90-day validation buffer (reduced price credits) during the pilot to mitigate ramp risk.

Next steps: can you confirm your target go-live quarter and who in procurement should receive the MSA/SOW? If this framing looks good I’ll circulate an updated SOW with the alternate 8-GPU min-floor scenario for procurement review.

Thanks —
Jonas Weber
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com | (415) 555-0127

Subject: Re: Dedicated reservation — sprint activation & minimal floor options

Jonas —

Thanks for the clear plan and the PDF. A few quick clarifying questions before we engage procurement: 

1) Economics: can you break the delta between the 12-GPU floor and the 8-GPU floor as an expected monthly run-rate? Our CFO will want a clear per-month cost delta including expected burst spend.
2) Warm-start / KV caching: how much of the cost reduction in month 2+ is attributable to caching vs reserved capacity? We're trying to understand the leverage points.
3) Flexibility: our internal validation cycle may push the production ramp by 4–6 weeks. How flexible is the ramp schedule and what are the contract change windows?

Procurement (cc): please confirm the correct contact for MSA ingestion and whether a PO will be required at signature.

Appreciate it —
Aisha Patel
Head of Platform Engineering | Terminus Bio
aisha.patel@terminusbio.com
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@terminusbio.com>
Cc: Dr. Ethan Shaw <ethan.shaw@terminusbio.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@terminusbio.com>
Date: Mon, 04 Jun 2028 15:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated reservation — sprint activation & minimal floor options

Aisha — thanks, good questions. Short answers here and I can expand in a 15m follow-up if useful.

1) Economics (monthly run-rate delta):
   - 12-GPU min floor (reserved): estimated committed charge = $72k/month.
   - 8-GPU min floor (reserved): estimated committed charge = $48k/month.
   - Typical burst/overage for pilot (expected): $4–8k/month if your traffic profile stays within the pilot lane; worst-case burst depends on model tokenization and inference length.
   - Net delta (12 vs 8): ~ $24k/month in committed spend, with burst smoothing likely to add ~10–15% additional variable spend during ramp windows.

2) Warm-start / KV caching: caching and prefix reuse typically reduce per-token runtime by ~18–30% for chat-style workloads. On our recommendations, ~40–60% of observed per-token cost improvements between pilot and steady-state come from caching + optimized batching, the rest from capacity scaling (i.e., reserved GPUs remove queueing overhead). We call out these savings in the SOW and provide per-route profiling in the Console so you can track regression.

3) Flexibility / change windows: standard contract allows two change windows per 12-month term with 30d notice for stage adjustments. For this pilot we can offer a one-time 14d soft-change buffer during the first 90 days (no penalty) to accommodate your validation lag.

I’ll attach an alternate SOW with the 8-GPU min-floor variant and an annotated cost sheet. If procurement confirms the correct intake address I’ll send the MSA/DocuSign link.

Best —
Jonas
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 04 Jun 2028 15:45:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: TERM-4891 — quick pricing / discount ask

Karthik / Ben —

Looping you both in with the Aisha thread above. Quick read: they prefer the lower min-floor (8 GPUs) for flexibility but we should protect latency SLAs with a shared burst pool and a 72-hour warm-start requirement before stage increases. Proposed commercial approach:

- Offer 8-GPU committed floor for the 12-month term to reduce CFO friction.
- Add 12k in prewarm credits (applied over first 90 days) to offset early burst costs.
- Approve a 10% net-first-year volume discount if they commit to the 48-GPU ramp plan by EOM Jun.

If finance wants to keep the committed amount higher, alternative is to keep the 12-GPU floor and add a smaller discount but I think this will slow signing. Thoughts?

Jonas
From: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@terminusbio.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@terminusbio.com>, Dr. Ethan Shaw <ethan.shaw@terminusbio.com>
Date: Wed, 06 Jun 2028 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated reservation — sprint activation & minimal floor options

Jonas —

Appreciate the breakdown — that helps. Procurement here: we will review the MSA and confirm PO requirements (procurement@terminusbio.com).

Terminus confirms we are willing to proceed with the 8-GPU minimum floor + 48-GPU staged ramp with the following asks:

- Please include the 72-hour warm-start clause and the 90-day validation buffer in the SOW.
- Apply the 12k prewarm credit against overage invoices for months 1–3.
- Provide the updated SOW and a DocuSign MSA link; procurement will route for internal signature.

Once I have the SOW I’ll circulate internally. Attaching a PO stub for intake.

Thanks —
Aisha Patel
